extracted.intended_audience: writers and artists submitting work to McSweeney’s 'Our Refrigerator Door' (readers/aspiring contributors)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines for submitting artwork, personal essays, short fiction, and poetry to McSweeney’s 'Our Refrigerator Door' column; emphasizes high-impact humor/creative work and physical submission constraints. Written in a humorous voice but specifies concrete formatting and content rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall editorial aim / impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Work should leave readers feeling invigorated and alive; provide a cathartic, life-altering experience and teach something about themselves and/or the world.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The site states: 'We want people to come away from our refrigerator door feeling invigorated and alive, as if they had just learned something about themselves and/or the world that heretofore they had not.' Because of this, we expect the best and only the best from those artists who wish to contribute their work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork: strength and boldness; meaningful realism or purposeful abstraction
rubrics_metrics.description: Artwork should be strong and bold; realism is preferred but abstract work is acceptable only if not abstract for its own sake and if the piece's artistic strength compels belief in its subject.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example guidance: 'You can say that squiggle in the corner of the page is a bunny, but we won’t believe it is a bunny unless the artistic strength of the piece compels us to believe it is a bunny. Having floppy ears and a bushy tail always helps, too.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork: physical weight/size constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Work must be light enough to be affixed to the refrigerator door by no more than six alphabet magnets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page: 'We are open to all types of media as long as the work is light enough to be affixed to our refrigerator door by no more than six alphabet magnets.' This is a hard physical constraint tied to display method.

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork: secure attachment of loose materials
rubrics_metrics.description: If including loose materials (e.g., uncooked pasta) make sure they are glued securely to prevent detachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidance and example: 'Collages are welcome, but if the piece of art contains uncooked pasta, make sure it is glued securely. Should an uncooked fusilli or farfalle detach and fall to the kitchen floor, our dog will attempt to eat it....' (practical/health/safety/cleanliness rationale given).

rubrics_metrics.name: Artwork: include identification and short description
rubrics_metrics.description: All artwork must include correct spelling of the artist's first name, date of creation, and a one- or two-line description of the piece.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: 'We realize some artists don’t like to include descriptions of their work... but we find descriptions essential because sometimes we have no idea what it is we’re looking at.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essays & fiction: powerful, affecting prose
rubrics_metrics.description: Written submissions must 'explode off the page' and strongly move the reader—pack prose with power, grace, and proper punctuation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exact wording: 'Your writing must explode off the page and render the reader your helpless, quivering slave... pack your prose with power, grace, and proper use of punctuation.' Emphasis on emotional/impactful writing quality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essays & fiction: punctuation discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Use punctuation (especially commas and exclamation points) wisely; do not scatter commas/exclamations carelessly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted guidance: 'Commas are not little playthings that you can leave here, there, and everywhere. So use them wisely or don’t use them at all. Same goes for exclamation points.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essays & fiction: physical submission format & appearance
rubrics_metrics.description: Prefer submissions on white-lined or yellow-lined paper with proper margins; work should look grown-up and not be scribbled haphazardly over the page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page: 'We prefer all written work to be submitted on either white-lined or yellow-lined paper... it's imperative that you use lined paper with proper margins. Far too often, we receive submissions that are nothing more than long scribbles written haphazardly over the entire page... we now require work that is aesthetically more grown-up-looking.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal essays & fiction: length and single-sided requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions must be no more than one page long and must be single-sided; double-sided work will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale: limited display space on refrigerator door—'There is only so much space to go around our refrigerator door... Double-sided work will not be considered. We don’t want readers lifting the work to view content on the other side of the paper.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Poetry: prohibition on 'poop' and variants
rubrics_metrics.description: Any poem containing the word 'poop' or its variations (e.g., 'poopy,' 'poopsicle,' 'pooptastic') will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rationale/alternative: 'No one wants to read about poop while standing at our refrigerator door. We recommend you submit your poopy poem to the bathroom wall instead.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Content prohibition: no robot-monkey-themed work
rubrics_metrics.description: The editors will not accept robot-monkey-themed drawings, stories, or other works; such submissions will be removed and not reinstated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: 'We are no longer accepting robot-monkey-themed work... Robot monkeys are so last July. And no saying that something is a tree and then later telling us it’s a robot monkey. That will lead to immediate removal from our refrigerator door, and no amount of crying and spinning wildly on the floor will make us put it back up.'

rubrics_metrics.name: No simultaneous submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not submit the same piece to more than one place at a time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page acknowledges other venues (family refrigerators, bulletin boards, lockers) but asks contributors to 'refrain from submitting to more than one place at a time.' Rationale: past turmoil over duplicate displays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-submission checklist (three questions)
rubrics_metrics.description: Before submitting, ensure: your name is spelled correctly; the submission is robot-monkey-free; the submission seeks to make a difference in people’s lives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicit three questions listed as a must-ask before submitting: 'Have I spelled my name correctly on my submission? Is my submission robot-monkey-free? Does my submission seek to make a difference in people’s lives?'

rubrics_metrics.name: Response time / expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Allow a one-to-three-minute response time; if editors are occupied (e.g., watching TV), expect a slightly longer wait.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quoted: 'Please allow a one-to-three-minute response time for your submission. If we are busy watching Prison Break, expect a slightly longer wait time.' (Humorous but serves as expectation-setting.)
